gauntlet: question
Reusing the resolver fits because the codebase already has one settings path. `settings/resolver.ts:12` owns the defaults, existing settings already flow through it, and I traced its resolved values to `ui/report-view.ts:30`, where the report view consumes them. A new setting there adds one default beside the others, and the view reads it the same way it reads everything else. A view-local settings object would put a second settings path beside the one that already owns every default. That splits where defaults live and adds a read path the view doesn't need today.

Next is behavior. Your report says filters stay active after a workspace switch and sometimes hide rows in the new workspace. Whether switching workspaces should reset filters is still undecided. What should switching workspaces do to report filters?
A) The new setting controls it: filters reset on workspace change by default, and users can opt to keep them.
B) Filters always reset on workspace change, with no setting for this. The new setting covers some other report-view behavior.
C) Filters always carry over, and the view shows a notice when active filters hide rows.
D) Other - name it.
Recommendation: A - the reset default fixes the hidden rows you reported, and the setting stays on the existing resolver path for anyone who wants filters to carry over.

gauntlet: question
Reusing the resolver fits because `settings/resolver.ts:12` already owns defaults, and `ui/report-view.ts:30` already consumes its resolved settings. The traced resolver-to-view path can carry the new setting without introducing a second settings object with separate defaults and synchronization responsibilities.

We’ll use that existing path. What should happen to report filters when the workspace changes?
A) Reset by default, with a setting to preserve filters instead.
B) Preserve filters by default, with a setting to enable resetting.
C) other - name it.
Recommendation: A - it directly prevents carried-over filters from unexpectedly hiding rows in the new workspace, while retaining an option for users who want persistence.
